title: The Island King and the Pious Traveler

keywords: the island king and the pious israelite
full_text:
A pious and honest merchant of the Levant embarked upon a sea voyage to trade in olive oil and cedarwood. A sudden hurricane shattered the vessel upon the reefs of a distant, uncharted ocean, and the merchant was cast ashore upon a lush, tropical island whose mountains rose like emerald spires from the sea.

As he walked along the beach, a company of horsemen bearing golden banners approached him. Instead of taking him captive, they dismounted, bowed to the earth, placed a royal crown upon his head, and conducted him to a magnificent marble palace!

The chief minister explained the ancient law of the island: 'Every year on this day, our previous monarch’s reign concludes, and we crown the first shipwrecked stranger who washes upon our shores as our sovereign for twelve months. For one year, your word is law; but when the year concludes, our boats will carry you to a barren, uninhabited rock in the northern sea to live in exile.'

The merchant listened with quiet discernment. He did not lose his head in banquets or luxurious dissipation.

Instead, during his twelve months of royal authority, he dispatched fleets of ships to that barren northern island, carrying fertile soil, seeds of date palms, builders, stonemasons, and engineers. They constructed reservoirs, planted lush orchards, and built a comfortable white palace beside a sheltered harbor.

When his year of rule ended, the islanders escorted him to the boat with customary ceremony, expecting him to weep. The merchant smiled with radiant peace.

When he reached the northern island, he stepped onto a blossoming paradise that his own foresight and industry had prepared! He was welcomed by the gardeners and fishermen he had settled there, living in abundance and peace, having learned that true wisdom prepares for the future while possessing the resources of the present.
moral: Honest character and faithful reliance on providence turn a shipwreck into an empire of justice.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
